name: npu_core_m3v
display_name: Magpie M3V NPU — cpu_m1-derived RISC-V+vector ML core, loosely-coupled to frozen cpu_m1 host over AXI
topology: two-core SoC: cpu_m1 (frozen host, main CPU) --AXI--> NPU core (cpu_m1-derived, modified). Loosely-coupled companion accelerator (CoralNPU-style), NOT tightly-coupled custom-0.
note: The NPU is a COPY of the frozen cpu_m1 scalar RTL (taken from tag m1a-rtl-freeze-v1.0) placed under IP/npu/ and MODIFIED to add ML compute (vector/GEMV/matrix EXU + local TCM + AXI slave/master). The frozen IP/cpu_m1/rtl/ is never touched. Route #5 (loosely-coupled) of docs/reports/m1a_performance_evaluation.md, but the companion is self-built from our own scalar rather than an Ethos-U-style fixed block or imported CoralNPU (that is the sibling M1V line).

isa_contract.source: CoralNPU datasheet parity (User directive 2026-07-03: match Google NPU first so the toolchain applies)
isa_contract.delta_vs_cpu_m1: add F (FPU) + Zve32x (vector); C dropped/optional (CoralNPU has no compressed)
isa_contract.config_parity: ITCM 8KB / DTCM 32KB, AXI4 master+slave, GEMV/matrix 64 MAC -> 256 (256 = datasheet matrix engine, NOT in open emit)

toolchain.goal: make the Google-NPU (open RVV) toolchain apply by matching the ISA contract
toolchain.honest_scope: Google coral-opt + CoralNPU IREE runtime are CLOSED (Synaptics Torq), unavailable here (M1V hit this, wrote stand-in m1v-coral-opt). What applies = standard OPEN RVV toolchain: clang -march=rv32imf_zve32x_zbb + RVV intrinsics + TFLM; M1V stand-in emitter as reference.
toolchain.golden: Spike ISS --isa rv32imf_zve32x (accepts zve32x locally); toolchain proven on ISS before RTL
toolchain.vector_lockstep_method: reuse M1V ADR-0028 RVV Zve32x vector-retire equivalence (reference)

host.core: IP/cpu_m1 (frozen M1A scalar @ m1a-rtl-freeze-v1.0) = main control CPU
host.existing_bus: cpu_m1_axil_top.v + axil_bridge.v already expose an AXI4-Lite master (valid-ready dmem bridged to AXI-Lite; vcformal-checked in flow/v2_pipeline/phase_p_axi). Control plane to the NPU works out of the box.
host.constraint: IP/cpu_m1/rtl/ must remain byte-identical to the freeze tag (host no-regression guard)

planned_units.name: npu_core
planned_units.role: cpu_m1 scalar spine (copied+modified) + F(FPU) as the NPU's control/sequencer core; runs ML kernels

planned_units.name: rvv_zve32x_exu
planned_units.role: standard RVV Zve32x vector EXU (VLEN=128, integer EEW<=32) — the ISA-parity vector unit

planned_units.name: gemv_matrix_engine
planned_units.role: int8/int4 GEMV/matrix array (start 64 MAC, path to 256; net-new, not in open CoralNPU emit)

planned_units.name: npu_tcm
planned_units.role: local ITCM/DTCM + 128-bit data path for weight/activation residency

planned_units.name: npu_axi_if
planned_units.role: AXI slave (host control/CSR + local-mem window) + AXI master (weight/activation DMA)

planned_units.name: axi_fabric
planned_units.role: interconnect + addr decode + AXI4-Lite(control) & AXI4-full+DMA(data, burst); net-new bus work

planned_units.name: soc_top
planned_units.role: two-core M3V SoC integration (host + NPU + fabric + shared mem)

verification.authority: SPLIT (route #5): host cpu_m1 = per-commit Spike lockstep (unchanged); NPU scalar spine = its own standalone Spike lockstep (cpu_m1-derived, so still Spike-golden); NPU vector/GEMV = Spike --extension or bit-accurate C golden model; boundary = AXI transaction scoreboard; system = ML e2e.
verification.note: Self-built NPU keeps the scalar part lockstep-able (advantage over the M1V imported-core route). The vector/GEMV extension is the only piece needing a new golden model. Document the split-authority deviation in the SKU contract.

planned_gates: gate_10_host_noregress (cpu_m1 frozen scalar re-verify, no new claim)
gate_20_axi_fabric (AXI4-Lite control + AXI4-full/DMA data; transaction scoreboard)
gate_30_npu_scalar_lockstep (cpu_m1-derived NPU scalar spine vs Spike)
gate_40_npu_gemv_cosim (vector/GEMV extension vs Spike --extension / C golden)
gate_50_two_core_ml_e2e (host orchestrates NPU: TFLM / int4 GEMV tinyLLM, roofline numbers)
